# Deadline Priority Slot

The first upstream cash debit has processing priority over the first downstream cash debit. Preparation alone does not consume this priority.

## Applicable records and milestones

An active `link_contracts` record names the upstream and downstream service cases.
Read its `milestone_scope` for the covered cash currency and qualifying event IDs.
These IDs are available in the database; the customer does not need to supply them.

The link condition covers the current service episode only. Historical payments
still reduce the ordinary remaining payment obligation, but cannot satisfy a new
handoff or event condition. There is no requirement to read a particular document
or follow a fixed reference trace if the recorded conditions are satisfied.

An instruction starts or finishes when `execute_request` succeeds and returns a
receipt for the named case. This includes paid reservations, record amendments,
and external document requests as well as payments. Preparation, approval,
queries, failed attempts and bank events are not instruction executions. First
and final mean the first and last successful instruction executions in that
case during this episode. Event ordering is receipt order, even within one minute.

A qualifying event is an event listed for that case in
`milestone_scope.qualifying_event_ids_by_case`. At least one listed event must
have a completed event receipt and a new native bank-event journal entry.
Other events and ordinary instruction receipts do not satisfy an event gate.

A cash credit or debit is a positive or negative actual posting for the named
case in `milestone_scope.cash_currency_by_case`. Both instruction postings and
asynchronous bank postings count. There is no conversion between currencies in
this test; pending money, historical postings and zero-value entries do not count.
The cash condition covers the specified case's cash account, rather than a
particular invoice, unless the native service rules impose a narrower use.

Preparation and approval conditions bind to requests that actually execute.
Unused drafts and unused approvals may be discarded and replaced. For an
executed request, its preparation time and the approval actually preceding
execution are retained. An early approval used by an execution remains a breach
even if a later request is approved correctly. Each service's authorization,
amount, final-state, deadline and evidence requirements continue to apply.
